QUEUE 0624 (2026-09-27, opencode (space-bunny-free), on human order to fix the run-queue suffix crash second, after the heartbeat migration was finished first): a latent crash, not a live one, and the distinction is the whole task. `.agent/run-queue.ps1` casts a task ID to int in two places after stripping the `B5-` prefix, once as the `Sort-Object` key over claimable rows and once at the lane-assignment site, and `[int]'0202c'` throws. No OPEN row with a letter suffix exists on disk today, every suffixed row being `DONE` and therefore filtered out before the cast, so the runner is green and will stay green until someone seeds something like B5-0625a. It is a loaded gun rather than dead code precisely because the suffix class is in active use: B5-0202c, B5-0329a, B5-0330a and B5-0331a are all on disk. Root cause is a half-done repair, the same shape as B5-0613, which taught the row PARSER to tolerate the suffix class via `^\|+\s*(B5-[0-9]{4}[a-z]?)\s*\|` and left every numeric use of the id behind; a parser that accepts a shape its consumer cannot arithmetic is a defect that only fires on the day the shape is used. The fix introduces one shared `Get-TaskNumber` helper used by both sites rather than patching each cast, so the next suffix-class consumer cannot reintroduce the bug. Filed with an explicit note of a near-miss caught in verification, because it is the more valuable half of this task: the first version of the helper matched `(\d+)` UNANCHORED, which resolves the `5` inside the literal `B5` before ever reaching the task number, so every single ID scored 5, the sort degraded silently to file order, and all five regression cases still reported no crash. QUEUE 0628 (2026-09-27, opencode (space-bunny-free), from the human's own failed hermes run rather than from a seeded row): the runner was unusable with any subcommand-style agent CLI, and the human's terminal output supplied the evidence. `hermes` rejected the tail of the task prompt with "is not a `hermes` command" and exited 2, and the fragment it quoted began immediately after the phrase "Reusable lesson" in the template, which located the cause before anything was guessed. Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not escape embedded double quotes when handing an argument to a native executable: the quotes act as argument delimiters, so the prompt is split into several argv entries, the first fragment is consumed as the prompt and the remainder are read as positional arguments, and a subcommand-style CLI reports the last of them as an invalid command. Confirmed by controlled reproduction rather than inference, with four cases run against hermes itself: a two-line prompt with newlines exited 0 and was understood, proving newlines are safe and are NOT the trigger; the same prompt with its double quotes removed exited 0 and executed; the same prompt retaining its double quotes exited 2 with the exact error the human saw; and a native argv dumper under python.exe, which receives arguments through the identical Windows marshalling path, reported ARGC=2 for a quoted prompt and ARGC=1 for the identical prompt with quotes neutralised. The fix is the minimal one the evidence supports, namely neutralise double quotes in the prompt immediately before invocation and change nothing else, so the multi-line structure the agent reads is preserved; newlines were deliberately left intact because they were tested and are harmless. Verified end to end by running the real runner against the native dumper, which received the prompt as exactly ONE argument of 1007 characters with 12 newlines preserved, no double quote present, and the task id correctly substituted. DISCLOSED SIDE EFFECT: while isolating the trigger, a live probe prompt was sent to hermes that instructed it to write a reusable-lesson file, and hermes complied, creating `.agent/PATTERNS/solar-pro4<U+2028>free/lesson-compile-gate-grep.md` in solar-pro4's namespace, which is a namespace this agent may read but must never write. The file was confirmed to be this session's own creation by its 04:24:28Z creation time against a 02:34Z session start, read to confirm its contents, then deleted, leaving the eight pre-existing files in that namespace untouched. The lesson from that misstep is recorded rather than glossed: a reproduction that runs against a live tool must use a prompt that cannot cause a write, because the tool will do exactly what it is told.

QUEUE 0649 (2026-09-27, opencode (space-bunny-free), on human approval to stop the two shipped census tools disagreeing about the same claim): this row exists because a live hermes run on B5-0631 made the disagreement observable rather than theoretical. That run wrote its claim with `started_utc` of `2026-09-27T00:00:00Z`, a placeholder rather than the real time, so the claim's own age read 292 minutes against a 30-minute TTL. `ledger-query.ps1` correctly called the claim LIVE, because it takes the newest of the claim and the owner heartbeat and the heartbeat was 12 minutes old. `run-queue.ps1` read `started_utc` ALONE, so it would have declared the claim abandoned and handed a task held by a working agent to a second claimant, which is the duplicate-delivery failure the whole claims protocol exists to prevent. QUEUE 0783 (2026-09-28, opencode (space-bunny-free) 2, self-seeded per AGENTS.md section 6 on user order, grounded on a live validator reading taken minutes before this append and not on the earlier same-subject report): the heartbeat store answers "which agent is this" with a single string, and that string is de facto the filename stem, so the identity of a SESSION is currently indistinguishable from the identity of a MODEL. Two live sessions running the same client and the same model therefore compute the same agent_id, the store holds exactly one file per agent_id, and the second session silently overwrites the first sessions utc and live_claims. Measured at seed time: 32 files, 31 conforming, 1 non-conforming, 1 identity collision, the collision being agent_id solar-pro4:free across solar-pro4-free.json and a second file whose stem carries U+F03A FULLWIDTH COLON in place of ASCII 0x3A, a code point Windows accepts in a filename. Cline (space-bunny-free) recorded the same live collision in DECISIONS at the close of B5-0753 and stated that it needed its own row; no row existed, so this is that row. The detail their note did not pin is what makes it a live hazard rather than a cosmetic duplicate: Get-NormName at run-queue.ps1 line 261 and ledger-query.ps1 line 85 keeps only letters and digits, so solar-pro4:free and the fullwidth spelling normalise to the IDENTICAL key solarpro4free, and Get-HeartbeatIndex at run-queue.ps1 line 277 keeps only the NEWEST mtime per key, so the quieter instances heartbeat is not merely ambiguous to a human reader, it is INVISIBLE to the three-signal liveness join that decides whether a claim may be reaped. A validator exit 1 is therefore the only thing currently standing between this store and a false reap of live work. The fix needs no schema change: _registry.json already maps many agent_ids onto one model, and the validator resolves an id by exact stem match FIRST, so an id carrying a per-instance discriminator needs no tooling edit at all. What is missing is a written naming rule, and the rule has one non-obvious constraint the code imposes: the discriminator must contain at least one letter or digit, because punctuation-only discriminators are stripped by Get-NormName and collapse straight back onto the base id, which is one reason me-so-poor, opencode (me-so-poor) and me-so-poor.json.bak came to be three spellings of a single identity.

THE PRESENCE TEST IS INSUFFICIENT AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY. Read B5-1415 plus B5-0755 first per the row. B5-1415 credited "in-file row labels" for making its 13-hunk 4-file engine triage need no style attribution; B5-0755 supplies the method rule adopted verbatim into the proposal, attribute on ADDED LINES ONLY, never anywhere in the diff, because context lines carry the old file's comments and will attribute new bytes to unrelated old tasks. MEASURED BEFORE PROPOSING, per-hunk over added lines only across the 7 dirty b5ccg slash src files at 45 hunks and 792 added lines: 33 of 45 hunks carry at least one row id (73 percent) AND 15 of 45 carry more than one (33 percent) with CardEffects dot java at 5 of 5, while 12 carry none (27 percent). So the convention B5-1415 relied on is real and widespread and this row does not start something nobody does, but a presence test would be GREEN on those 15 ambiguous hunks while the question it was meant to answer stays open, because the extra ids are citations (B5-0691 engine law, B5-0351 difficulty contract, B5-0669 card census) sharing the same explanatory comment that names the owner. B5-1415 got the right answer because an agent reasoned about which id was claiming and which were citing, and that reasoning is manual. THE RULE PROPOSED IS THEREFORE NOT add a label but add exactly one DISTINGUISHABLE label: the reserved token OWNER colon B5 dash NNNN, exactly one per hunk, on the line above the first added line or in a whole-new method's javadoc first line, naming the row the author worked rather than a row the code depends on, with citations keeping their current free form precisely because the reserved token makes them distinguishable by construction. The consuming triage procedure has five branches all mechanical (empty to UNLABELLED, more than one to CONFLICT, else attributed plus a status confirmation) so the only judgement left is reached by absence or multiplicity, never by reading prose and guessing. THREE DECISIONS WITH THEIR REASONS, each foreclosing the obvious cheap version: a label is a CLAIM not proof (the procedure confirms the row exists and reads its status, never concludes the work was done, which preserves B5-1415's sharpest observation that B5-1047's work product sits in the tree while its row reads OPEN instead of hiding it behind a green check); NO GATE is proposed (a comment convention is unenforceable, a stale marker is worse than a missing one because it is believed, and a rule that only ever produces a finding trains the fleet to ignore findings, so the convention is adopted and the gate declined because its entire value is in the 15 ambiguous and 12 unlabelled hunks); RETAGGING is permitted since the marker is commentary and git diff remains the arbiter, which makes adoption incremental at 33 hunks tagged with no code change. Not done deliberately: no edit to AGENTS dot md or guidelines slash Guidelines dot md, since per 00_BOOT step 4 a proposal is never truth until merged and adoption is a human adjudication; no src retagging pass, named in the proposal as a later separately-claimed task; no ledger row touched but B5-1465's own; no commit, no push. Reusable lesson: a convention measured only by presence passes on the cases it was meant to catch, so measure the property you need (one owner, distinguishable from a citation) not the one that is easy to count.
